text:
nora: Newton Labs dropped two LoRA adapters + a tiny tokenizer BPE tweak into intake. Can we run a short compatibility + quant smoke? They want float32/int8/int4 comparisons and a minimal repro if anything looks off.

david: Sure. What base + adapter order? Any known tokenizer intent?

neora: Base is gptx-7b-cust. Apply adapters in order: frankie_dialog.lora then numbers-instruct.lora. Tokenizer tweak adds a merged token for "."+digit (e.g., ".5") to optimize decimals.

keith: Heads-up: merging punctuation with digits can change attention patterns for decimal parsing. Also confirm adapter key namespaces don't collide; we've seen LoRA merges overwrite the same parameter slices if creators reused prefixes.

zoe: Smoke checklist from product: 1) tokenization roundtrip on 1k finance examples, 2) perplexity baseline float32 vs int8 vs int4, 3) per-prompt top-1 probability diffs (flag > 0.12), 4) short numeric reasoning probe (10 Qs), 5) embedding cos-sim vs 5 refs (mean/std), 6) adapter param overlap check + KV warmstart.

david: I'll assemble 24 prompts: 8 dialog, 8 numeric reasoning (decimals/currencies), 8 edge cases (locale separators). Will run float32 -> int8 -> int4, collect token_probs, embeddings, and adapter param name diffs.

ci-bot: CI queued: run/newton-merge-3370011222

david: Local run command:

```
python ci/eval_pack.py \
  --model gptx-7b-cust \
  --adapters frankie_dialog.lora,numbers-instruct.lora \
  --tokenizer-patch newton_bpe.json \
  --quants float32,int8,int4 \
  --prompts newton_smoke_prompts.json \
  --warmstart-prefix "[kv-ws]" \
  --collect token_probs,embeddings,param_names \
  --out s3://redwood-ci/newton/3370011222/results.zip
```

ci-bot: CI started: run/newton-merge-3370011222 -> setup

ci-bot: CI finished: SUCCESS. Artifacts: s3://redwood-ci/newton/3370011222/results.zip

david: Quick summary from artifacts:
- prompt_05 (decimal reasoning): top-1 shift float32->int4 = 0.26 (token split caused ".5" -> "." + "5")
- prompt_11 (locale test): top-1 shift = 0.14 (comma vs dot handling changed)
- numeric probe accuracy: float32 8/10 correct, int8 8/10, int4 6/10
- embedding cos-sim for numeric subset: mean 0.95 (float32) -> 0.88 (int4)
- adapter param name diff: both LoRAs defined custom_prefix "ln_1" -> namespace collision detected for ~2k params (overlap risk).

keith: Namespace collision could cause weight blending in unexpected places. That plus tokenizer BPE change explains degraded numeric outputs in int4. We should flag both issues separately.

zoe: Triage plan: 1) recommend int8 as production fallback until both tokenizer and prefix fixes land, 2) ask Newton to rename adapter prefixes (make them unique) or we offer automatic prefix-scope isolation, 3) request tokenizer BPE to preserve dot-leading decimals as single token for locales in their dataset or provide a pre-tokenize mapping.

nora: Can someone prepare minimal repro bundle (prompts 05 & 11 + token traces + param diff) and upload? We'll include recommended mitigations in the customer note.

david: Uploaded repro + traces + param-diff: s3://redwood-ci/newton/3370011222/repro_05_11_bundle.tar.gz

ci-bot: Artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-ci/newton/3370011222/repro_05_11_bundle.tar.gz

keith: I'll draft a short internal mitigation: add a pre-ingest adapter isolation step in the runtime to remap adapter prefixes, and add a tokenizer policy to keep dot+digit atomic as an opt-in. Will open PRs for tests.

zoe: I'll draft the account note: summary, artifacts, recommended short-term mitigation (int8 + adapter rename), and timeline for tokenizer/namespace fixes. Will loop in AE once we confirm PR ETAs.

nora: Thanks team  good quick loop. Follow-ups: keith to open adapter-isolation test PR, david to run a focused int4 rerun after isolation shim (if we push it), zoe to send customer note. Close when PRs are in. :email:
